# Testing a program at the console

<!-- Generated by tools/generate-docs.lisp from docs/skill/: do not edit by hand. -->

Use this for a program that talks to a person: a REPL, `ask`, `confirm` or
`choose`. Its output alone does not show it working, because those prompts read
keys in a real console, and your shell gives a program a pipe instead.

`tools/console_driver.py` in the cog-lisp folder runs a program in a real
console and types at it from a script you write.

## Set it up once

- Windows: `python -m pip install --user pywinpty pyte`
- Linux: `python3 -m pip install --user ptyprocess pyte`

Run it with `python`, not `python -I`: `-I` hides those packages.

## Write a script

One step a line; `#` starts a comment.

```
expect weather>
send ask (berlin needs-a-coat yes)
expect [y/N]
type y
expect Yes
send (car '())
expect error:
key eof
exit 0
```

- `send TEXT` types TEXT and Enter. `type TEXT` types it alone.
- `key NAME [N]` presses a key N times: `enter`, `up`, `down`, `tab`, `esc`,
  `ctrl-c`, or `eof`, the end of input.
- `expect TEXT` waits until TEXT is printed after your last input. A missing
  TEXT fails the script. `expect-re` takes a Python regex.
- `expect-screen TEXT` waits for TEXT on the screen as drawn;
  `expect-screen-re` takes a regex, `^` at a line's start.
- `refute TEXT` fails if TEXT was printed after your last input.
- `print` shows what was printed after your last input.
- `exit 0` waits for the program to end with that code.

A yes/no question (`confirm`) takes one key: `type y`, not `send y`.

## Run it

- Windows: `python tools/console_driver.py test.txt -- cmd.exe /c .\cog-lisp.bat program.lisp`
- Git Bash: the same, with `cmd.exe //c`
- Linux: `python3 tools/console_driver.py test.txt -- ./cog-lisp.sh program.lisp`

Give the scripts and programs as paths from where you run it, or give
`--cwd`. It prints `passed` and exits 0. On a failure it prints the step, what
was printed, and the screen. `--transcript FILE` keeps all the output.
